extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO (particularly those handling trademark and non-patent matters); OED staff and USPTO disciplinary stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, legal provisions, procedures, and sanctions used by the USPTO (Office of Enrollment and Discipline and Director) to evaluate and resolve attorney misconduct in trademark and other non-patent matters, including jurisdictional bases, specific rule violations, sanctioning, and publication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary proceedings pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. § 11.19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the statutory/regulatory authority under which the Director and OED may approve settlement agreements and impose discipline for practitioner misconduct before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Code and Rules by date
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct are applicable in this investigation: the Code applies to conduct prior to May 3, 2013, and the Rules apply to conduct on or after May 3, 2013 (see 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.20–10.112 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101–11.901).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating practitioner conduct, identify which regime (Code vs. Rules) applies based on the date(s) of the conduct; both may be referenced in investigations spanning the changeover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct involving dishonesty or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in misconduct involving dishonesty or misrepresentation in a client matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent acknowledged that, based on stipulated facts, her conduct violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4). The factual example here is repeatedly telling a client an application was being processed when it had not been filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglecting a client matter entrusted to the practitioner (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Neglect of a client matter entrusted to the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent admitted violation of 10.77(c) based on failure to timely file a client's trademark application and generally failing to perform legal services with competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to act with reasonable diligence and promptness (37 C.F.R. § 11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where, for example, Respondent failed to file a trademark application within two years after being retained to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonesty or misrepresentation under the Rules (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in misconduct involving dishonesty or misrepresentation (per Rules), e.g., misinforming a client on multiple occasions about filing status when the application had not been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to evaluate repeated misrepresentations to a client about the status of a matter; the document cites four separate occasions of false status responses as the basis for this violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior public discipline as a rule violation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Being publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by a duly constituted authority of a State constitutes a basis for discipline under the Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner's state-court discipline (here, a California suspension and stayed suspension with terms) is expressly a factor/violation under the USPTO Rules and may be the basis for USPTO action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposed suspension from practice before the Office (sanction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall be suspended from practice before the Office in trademark and other non-patent matters for a specified period (here, sixty (60) days) commencing on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions can be time-limited suspensions tailored to the misconduct; the order sets the suspension period and scope (trademark/non-patent matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedure and petition requirement (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended until the OED Director grants a petition requesting reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspended practitioners must follow the regulatory procedure and meet any requirements under § 11.60 before resuming practice in the suspended matter areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation upon reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon reinstatement, the respondent shall serve a probationary period (here, two years) commencing on the date of reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Probation is an additional supervisory discipline term after reinstatement; during probation the OED Director monitors compliance with the Final Order and the Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order-to-Show-Cause procedure for probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If OED believes the respondent violated the Final Order or Rules during probation, OED shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to respondent's last address of record, grant 15 days to respond, and if still unsatisfied, deliver materials to the USPTO Director and request immediate suspension for up to an additional 24 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lays out the stepwise procedural mechanism for escalating discipline during probation: (1) Order to Show Cause; (2) service at last address; (3) 15 days to respond; (4) submission to the USPTO Director requesting further suspension up to 24 months. The OED may also seek further discipline by other means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-abatement of suspension pending review
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director suspends the respondent pursuant to the Order to Show Cause and the respondent seeks review of that suspension, such review shall not operate to postpone or hold the suspension in abeyance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspensions ordered under this procedure take effect immediately and are not stayed by a review request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 as ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly requires respondent's compliance with § 11.58 (the order does not restate § 11.58's text, but imposes the regulatory obligation as a term of discipline).

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order imposes procedural/publication/administrative duties on the OED Director as required by the cited regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and notice of suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in the OED's FOIA Reading Room and publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette containing the practitioner's name, location, the suspension order, the violated rules, and factors reflected in the resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must identify the violations (by citation), describe the sanction, and may note mitigating/aggravating factors (e.g., no prior USPTO discipline; cooperation). Publication supports transparency and public notice of discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in agreed-upon resolution (mitigating/aggravating)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors reflected in the agreed-upon resolution include (i) no prior disciplinary history before the USPTO, and (ii) full cooperation with the OED during investigation and resolution of the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigating factors such as no prior history and cooperation are explicitly noted as influencing the sanction in settlement; such factors can reduce discipline severity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of this disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding (including the Final Order) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of similar misconduct; and in any future disciplinary proceeding the record may be used (i) as an aggravating factor to determine discipline and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by or on respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior discipline is explicitly available to the Office for future enforcement and credibility assessment; respondents should expect the record to be used in that manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs arising from the proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the Agreement and the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement terms may specify that each party bears its own costs rather than imposing monetary costs or restitution as part of the sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreement approval and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A Proposed Settlement Agreement resolving all disciplinary action arising from stipulated facts may be submitted to and approved by the USPTO Director; upon approval, the Agreement resolves the disciplinary action and the Final Order sets forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document demonstrates that consensual settlements between respondent and OED can fully resolve disciplinary matters, subject to Director approval and public posting.
